params.body:
Makes model comparisons mean something before any phase moves. No phase default changes.

## Why

The gold-set runs of 2026-10-10 ranked models by plain POEM accuracy. Three things made that ranking unreliable:

- **The gold set is three quarters 'earned'** (39,860 of about 53,200 rows). A model that answers 'earned' to everything scores 75%. Haiku 4.5 (66%), Mistral Large 3 (68%) and Llama 3.3 (76%) were all at or below that line. Haiku 5.5's 90% may partly be a lean toward 'earned'.
- **Each run drew its own 50 random rows**, so part of every gap between two models was a gap between two samples.
- **The judge needs a third family** once Model B may become Mistral.

## What changes

- **`eval-metrics.mjs`**, new. For POEM it records:
  - a confusion matrix per type;
  - balanced accuracy, the mean recall per type, which puts always-'earned' at 25%;
  - Cohen's kappa, which puts always-'earned' at 0;
  - recall and precision per type, with 'peer' visible on its own because it weighs most downstream.

  All of it is stored in `model_evals.details` and printed under each run.
- **Leaderboard**
  - Ranked by balanced accuracy, with kappa beside it. Older runs without it sort below.
  - Optional `--since` date, and a signals column.
- **`eval-models` options** (parsed in `eval-args.mjs`):
  - `--n` sets the sample size.
  - `--lang` limits the draw to one language.
  - `--seed` gives every model the same rows.
  - `--balanced` takes the same number of rows of each POEM type.
  - `--since` limits the leaderboard to runs from a date.

  The script now loads `.env` itself, as the supervisor does. Before, the Mistral and Together keys were only there in a shell where someone had loaded `.env` by hand, and in any other shell every batch failed with "not set".

  A seeded or balanced draw picks from the ids first and then reads only the chosen rows. The full eligible set is some fifty thousand texts, too much to hold in memory next to the running pipeline.
- **Catalog**
  - Mistral Medium 3.5 (`mistral-medium-2604`) and Z.ai GLM 5.3 (`zai-glm-5-3`, served by Mistral on the EU endpoint). Ids are as the endpoint's `/v1/models` listed them; prices are list × 1.1.
  - The first-run results are noted next to Small 4 and Large 3.
- **Docs**
  - The defaults table in CLAUDE.md said Sonnet for classify while the code ran Haiku. It now points at `DEFAULTS`.
  - The verify-tier note and the `consensus.mjs` header no longer name DeepSeek.

## How it was tested

- New tests:
  - `eval-metrics`: always-'earned' scores 75% plain but 25% balanced with kappa 0; a model that reads every type ties on plain accuracy and is told apart; capitals and unknown labels are handled.
  - `eval-args`: options, seeded and balanced draws, the id-first queries.
  - `eval-leaderboard`: `since`, and ranking by balanced accuracy.
  - The catalog ids.
- Smoke-tested on a fixture database: `--balanced --n 8` drew two rows of each type through the id-first path.
- `npm test`: 1114 pass, 6 fail. The six are `report-render`, which fails the same way on main because the workbench has no `pdftoppm`.

## After merge, on the box

```bash
for m in "" claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5 mistral/mistral-large-2512 together/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo mistral/zai-glm-5-3; do
  node packages/engine/eval-models.mjs classify $m --balanced --n 100 --seed 7
done
node packages/engine/eval-models.mjs leaderboard classify --since 2026-10-11
```
params.title: Measure models fairly: POEM beyond the earned share, same signals per model, Medium 3.5 and GLM 5.3
